name: Kavesk

anatomy.part: nose of the kite, where the bridle is tied on the spine (the star sits on the spine just above the cross spar, and the kite's apex is drawn above it)
left wingtip of the kite (torn tip)
right wingtip of the kite (far tip)
bottom point of the kite, where the cord is knotted on
knot in the cord, tied into a small two-loop bow with a short tail
loose cut end of the cord, frayed into splayed strands

myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up but did not come all the way free. A short length of cord stayed knotted to his hand, and it still hangs at the bottom of the Unflown: a kite with its loose end trailing down past everything else. Mother Hesk counted the turns on her Reel and found one missing, and she has never forgiven the wind for it. Tavo laughs when he passes the kite, and he cannot be asked to tie it back. Sailors who lose the Leeward Reach in fog are told to follow the cord, because it runs toward the place where the string was cut and the sky can still be reached. Ennu says a kite cut loose can be mended and flown again, though Ennu says many things over a needle. Sil looks along that cord every night for her brother, and finds only the hanging end.
verse:
Loose cord, hanging down,
no hand holds the other end.
Follow it, sailor.
